title: Plane crash off coast of Mississippi kills six, including two children
summary:
Divers recover bodies after Cessna 210 went down in Gulf of Mexico on Tuesday afternoon killing all onboard

Divers have found the bodies of six people killed in

blocks.text: Divers have found the bodies of six people killed in a small plane crash on Tuesday off the coast of Mississippi, according to the US Coast Guard.

Their bodies were in the plane’s fuselage after the Cessna 210 went down in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island, which is part of the Gulf Islands national seashore. Four adults and two boys, ages eight and 10, were onboard, a Coast Guard spokesperson, Juan Ros, said.

The air traffic control regional tower in Mobile, Alabama, reported about 3.45pm that it lost contact with the aircraft, according to the Coast Guard. Responders searched for hours and initially only found three lifejackets, a life raft and the plane’s cabin floating on the water, according to Ros.
The Cessna was en route from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida, according to the flight tracking website FlightAware.
Cmdr Trevor Blount, the Coast Guard coordinator for search and rescue in the Mobile area, called the situation heartbreaking.

“While this is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, we are grateful for the strong interagency coordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families,” he said in a statement.
The New Orleans news station WVUE reported that those onboard the crashed plane were traveling back home after a fishing trip in Venice, Louisiana.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) will investigate the crash.
On 3 November, a Learjet 60 business jet nosedived into the ground in south Florida, killing all nine people on board. The terrifying crash was captured on video recorded by people inside their cars.
